item.title: China-Pakistan Joint Army Training Enters Multi-subject Live-force Phase
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-21
KORLA, Oct. 21-- The China-Pakistan "Karakoram-2026" joint army training exercise has entered the multi-subject live-force training exercise phase. Throughout the exercise, both sides' participating troops were divided into multiple mixed teams for coordinated actions, shared weapons and equipment, and achieved unified command. During the assault operations, the mixed teams conducted tactical drills including providing security, bounding, and the handling of emerging threats. In addition, military medics from both sides conducted joint training on high-altitude tactical combat casualty care, sharing practical first-aid experience. (Video Editor: Zhang Jinwen)

item.title: Xi stresses prioritizing ecological conservation, pursuing green development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, visits the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve in Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, Oct. 16, 2026. Xi made an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) ULANQAB, Inner Mongolia, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has emphasized the need to unswervingly follow the path of prioritizing ecological conservation and pursuing green development. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. Huangqihai Lake in Ulanqab was once on the verge of drying up due to climate and other impacts. After years of comprehensive conservation, its water body has gradually been restored and expanded. During the inspection trip, Xi visited the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve, where he was briefed on Inner Mongolia's efforts to strengthen ecological conservation, and inspected the lake's shoreline and mudflats and observed birds inhabiting the area. He stressed the need to fully implement the country's wetland protection law, firmly uphold ecological red lines, and safeguard biodiversity. For degraded wetland ecosystems, he called for giving priority to natural restoration, supplemented by human intervention, and carrying out restoration in a scientific and sound manner. Xi visited Chahar High Tech Development Zone in Ulanqab, and learned about Inner Mongolia's progress in advancing the construction of a hub for the "East Data, West Computing" project and the development of the green computing power industry. Noting that implementing the "East Data, West Computing" project and building a national integrated computing power network is an important decision made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi stressed the need to ensure the efficient operation of completed projects and finish the construction of follow-up projects on schedule. He called on all parties to earnestly implement the requirements for efficient, green and safe development, actively promote the development of the green computing power industry, and make greater contributions to building Digital China and developing new quality productive forces. Xi also viewed displays of local agricultural and livestock specialties, encouraging local authorities to better align production with sales to help farmers and herders increase their incomes. item.title: Only by thoroughly reflecting on its past and sincerely repenting can Japan truly face the future: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 -- "Only by thoroughly reflecting on its past and sincerely repenting can Japan truly face the future," said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a press briefing on Friday. The spokesperson made the remarks when commenting on the war crimes of the notorious Unit 731 of the Imperial Japanese Army. According to reports, the Singaporean documentary Inside Unit 731: Japan's Secret Human Experiments received Singapore's national award for the Best History Documentary, with 1.45 million views on YouTube. Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK) aired the documentary A Secret Unit: The Silent Postwar Era, which exposes Unit 731's crimes against humanity through newly discovered photographs, firsthand testimony and other evidence. The spokesperson pointed out that during World War II, the Unit 731 conducted appalling humane experiments and waged biological warfare in China. These heinous crimes gravely violated international law. The extent of their crimes against humanity is beyond description, marking one of the darkest chapters in the history of human civilization. He further noted that right-wing forces in Japan have recently used emerging technologies to "poison" data in an attempt to whitewash Japan's culpability for its aggression and distort public perceptions, once again triggering high vigilance within the international community. "As some insightful people in Japan have pointed out, historical truth cannot be erased, and the crimes committed by the Japanese forces during their invasion of China are backed by irrefutable evidence and cannot be denied," stressed the spokesperson.

item.title: China Will Take Effective Measures to Deter Any Sabotaging Moves in South China Sea: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
BEIJING, Oct. 16 -- "The Chinese side will take resolute and effective measures to deter any sabotaging moves in the South China Sea, and uphold regional peace and stability," said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a press conference on October 16, 2026. According to media reports, the Philippine side recently made provocations near Huangyan Dao and Ren'ai Jiao multiple times and said that it would not allow the Chinese side to dictate terms on Philippine "territory". The Philippine military claimed that they observed over a hundred Chinese warships and China Coast Guard vessels maintaining regular presence in waters near Zhongye Dao and Xianbin Jiao, and that the Chinese side intended to shake the Philippines' resolve in safeguarding its rights and interests. "China has indisputable sovereignty over Huangyan Dao and Nansha Qundao, including Zhongye Dao, Xianbin Jiao and Ren'ai Jiao, and their adjacent waters, and has sovereign rights and jurisdiction over relevant waters," said the spokesperson. The spokesperson pointed out: "These islands and reefs lie outside the scope of Philippine territories. Therefore the Philippine side is not qualified to claim 'safeguarding its own rights and interests'." "The Chinese side takes necessary measures in accordance with laws and regulations to uphold its sovereign rights. They are legitimate, reasonable, professional and standardized," the spokesperson added. "For some time, the Philippine side has been rallying external forces to stir up troubles in the South China Sea at the expense of the common interests of regional countries. It continues to make provocations violating others' sovereignty and distort facts to spread false narratives, which makes itself a destroyer of peace and a destabilizing factor in the South China Sea," the spokesperson noted.

item.title: Xi's article on advancing Party self-governance to be published
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15
BEIJING, Oct. 15 (Xinhua) -- An article by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance with higher standards and more concrete measures, will be published on Friday. The article by Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, will be published in this year's 20th issue of the Qiushi Journal, a flagship magazine of the CPC Central Committee. It calls for upholding and strengthening overall Party leadership and persistently advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance to turn the blueprint drawn up at the fourth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee into reality. It stresses that the Party Central Committee's major policy decisions and arrangements must be implemented with stronger determination and vigor. It also demands strengthening concrete, targeted and regular oversight of the implementation of strategic initiatives, such as applying the new development philosophy, promoting high-quality development, and accelerating the building of a new development paradigm. The article requires more scientific and effective efforts to confine power to an institutional cage. It highlights that everyone is equal before laws and regulations, with no exemptions or special privileges when observing and enforcing these rules. The article says that the fight against corruption must be pursued with greater sobriety and resolve. It describes the anti-corruption campaign as a high-stakes struggle that cannot be lost, requiring an unswerving high-pressure posture to be maintained. It further demands the timely detection, accurate identification and effective resolution of all forms of corruption, with refined anti-corruption mechanisms that align oversight actions across all sectors.
